body:
## Quick answer

At a Nepali wedding, female guests traditionally wear a **saree** or a **kurta suruwal** (a kurta with trousers and a shawl or dupatta). For the reception, an **Anarkali, lehenga or festive gown** is very common. Choose **bright, happy colours** like pink, green, yellow, orange, maroon or royal blue. **Red is the bride's colour**, so most guests choose other shades. Avoid **all white** and **all black**, which many families link with mourning.

This guide is for guests at Nepali weddings in Nepal and in Nepali communities in the USA, the UK, Australia, Canada and the Gulf.

*By the Bahe Kurtiz styling team, Jaipur. Every piece is stitched in our own Jaipur unit.*

## The events of a Nepali wedding

Customs differ between communities (Bahun-Chhetri, Newar, Gurung, Magar, Tharu and others), but a Hindu Nepali wedding often includes:

| Event | What happens | What to wear |
|---|---|---|
| Mehendi / haldi (in many modern weddings) | Henna and turmeric for the bride and groom | Bright kurta set or Anarkali |
| Janti | The groom's family and friends arrive in a procession, often with panche baja music | Festive saree or kurta suruwal |
| Wedding ceremony (biha) | Rituals such as kanyadan and sindoor, led by a priest | Saree or kurta suruwal |
| Bidaai | The bride leaves for the groom's home | Same as the ceremony |
| Reception | Dinner and dancing, often the next day | Anarkali, lehenga, gown or glamorous saree |

## What to wear to the ceremony

The ceremony is the most traditional part. A **silk or georgette saree** is the classic choice. If you do not wear sarees, a **kurta suruwal or kurta set with a dupatta** is perfect and easy to sit in during long rituals. Choose something modest with sleeves.

## What to wear to the reception

The reception is more glamorous and modern. An **Anarkali suit or gown**, a **lehenga**, or a **designer saree** all work. Embroidery, sequins and shimmer are welcome in the evening.

## Colours to wear and avoid

**Lucky and popular colours:** pink, magenta, green, yellow, orange, maroon, royal blue, teal.

**Avoid:**
- **Bridal red** at the ceremony, as the bride usually wears red
- **All white**, which is linked with mourning in Nepali Hindu culture
- **All black**, which many older relatives consider unlucky at weddings

## Jewellery and accessories

Married Nepali women often wear the **pote** (a green or red glass bead necklace) and **tilhari**, but guests do not need these. Simple gold or kundan earrings, bangles and a **tika** or bindi will look lovely with any outfit.

## Winter weddings abroad

Nepali weddings in the USA, UK and Australia often happen in cooler months. Wear a **warm shawl or a long coat** over your saree or Anarkali between venues, and choose **velvet** for evening events.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can a non-Nepali guest wear a saree to a Nepali wedding?**
Yes. Most families love it when guests wear traditional clothes. If draping a saree is difficult, a kurta suruwal or Anarkali with a dupatta is just as respectful.

**Can I wear red to a Nepali wedding as a guest?**
It is best to avoid bright bridal red at the ceremony. A deep maroon or a red-and-gold mix is usually fine at the reception.

**What is kurta suruwal?**
Kurta suruwal is a traditional Nepali outfit: a long tunic (kurta) worn with loose trousers (suruwal) and usually a shawl or dupatta. It is similar to an Indian kurta set.

**Is white OK at a Nepali wedding?**
Avoid an all-white outfit. White with bright embroidery or colourful prints is usually fine.
